column1: # Per-position exceptions for BnF Dupuy 468 f.28r-v, 23 September 2026 (ASSIGNMENTS row 25).
# key.tsv gives one dominant value per cipher symbol, from the majority of the interlinear gloss's
# aligned letters (key_from_gloss.py, votes in key_from_gloss.tsv). At the 10 positions below, the
# gloss word actually written over that token disagrees with the symbol's dominant value -- a minority
# vote (NOTES.md "Self-consistency": 9 single-letter-type minority votes, plus the r04 word-sign case
# discussed separately in the Grading table). check.py applies this table as a per-position override so
# reading.txt carries what the gloss itself says at these ten spots, not the mechanically-applied
# majority key. Every row here is graded H (rule 4: read from a key source -- the gloss, on the document
# itself, at that exact position), not S or M.
# The gloss_value column is what check.py substitutes for key.tsv's value at that (line, pos): a bare
# letter merges into the surrounding cipher run as usual; '=word' renders as a bracketed word-sign
